records.source: וַיִּקְח֞וּ כָּל־עַ֤ם יְהוּדָה֙ אֶת־עֻזִּיָּ֔הוּ וְה֕וּא בֶּן־שֵׁ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָ֑ה וַיַּמְלִ֣יכוּ אֹת֔וֹ תַּ֖חַת אָבִ֥יו אֲמַצְיָֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And took all [the] people of Judah Uzziah, and he [was] a son of sixteen year[s], and they made king him in place of his father Amaziah.
pieces: Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, then sixteen years old, and made him king to succeed his father Amaziah.

L.1: And all the people of Judah took Uzziah, and he [was] sixteen years old, and they made him king in place of his father Amaziah.

R.1: Then all the people of Judah chose Uzziah, Amaziah's son, and made him king in his father's place. Uzziah was sixteen years old.

decisions.choice: Uzziah: the king Kings mostly calls Azariah
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 2 Kings 14:21 word for word, except that Kings names the king Azariah. Kings uses both names (Azariah in 2 Kings 15:1-8; Uzziah in 15:13, 30-34); Chronicles and the prophets use Uzziah (Isaiah 1:1; 6:1; Hosea 1:1; Amos 1:1). The names are close in meaning, "Yahweh has helped" and "Yahweh is my strength", and both name the same king. Each verse keeps the name it uses; in this chapter Azariah is also the name of the priest who stands against the king (verses 17 and 20).

decisions.choice: all the people of Judah: the nation acting together
decisions.reason: Amaziah had been killed by plotters at Lachish (25:27-28). The people, not the plotters, chose the next king, and they chose Amaziah's son, so David's line went on.

decisions.choice: a son of sixteen years: sixteen years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years.

decisions.choice: took (Balanced); chose (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 14:21 is kept at each level, with the name Uzziah. Readable says "chose" for "took", names him as Amaziah's son and gives his age in a sentence of its own.

records.heading: Uzziah king of Judah

records.source: ה֚וּא בָּנָ֣ה אֶת־אֵיל֔וֹת וַיְשִׁיבֶ֖הָ לִֽיהוּדָ֑ה אַחֲרֵ֥י שְׁכַֽב־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עִם־אֲבֹתָֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: He built Eloth and restored it to Judah, after lay down the king with his fathers.
pieces: It was he who rebuilt Eloth and won it back for Judah, after King Amaziah had rested with his ancestors.

L.2: He built Eloth and restored it to Judah, after the king lay down with his fathers.

R.2: After his father Amaziah died, Uzziah rebuilt the town of Eloth and made it part of Judah again.

decisions.choice: Eloth: the town Kings calls Elath
decisions.reason: This verse repeats 2 Kings 14:22. The only difference is the spelling of the town's name: Kings has Elath, Chronicles Eloth, as in 8:17. It was Judah's port at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba, near Ezion-geber (1 Kings 9:26), lost when Edom broke away (21:8-10).

decisions.choice: he: Uzziah; the king: Amaziah
decisions.reason: The stressed pronoun "he" points to Uzziah. "The king" who lay down with his fathers is Amaziah: Uzziah won the town back after his father's death, finishing what Amaziah's victory over Edom had begun (25:11-12).

decisions.choice: built: rebuilt, fortified
decisions.reason: The town already existed; "build" here means to rebuild and strengthen it.

decisions.choice: It was he (Balanced); Amaziah; Uzziah
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 14:22, Balanced shows the stress on "he" and names King Amaziah; Readable names both kings so the reader does not confuse them, and says "died" for the death formula.

records.source: בֶּן־שֵׁ֨שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ עֻזִּיָּ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וַחֲמִשִּׁ֤ים וּשְׁתַּ֨יִם֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ יְכָלְיָ֖ה מִן־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: A son of six-teen year[s] [was] Uzziah when he became king, and fifty and two year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem; and [the] name of his mother [was] Jecoliah from Jerusalem.
pieces: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah; she was from Jerusalem.

L.3: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and fifty-two years he reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [was] Jecoliah from Jerusalem.

R.3: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for fifty-two years. His mother was Jecoliah from Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: as 2 Kings 15:2, with the name Uzziah
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 2 Kings 15:2, but names the king, Uzziah, where Kings says "he". Chronicles leaves out the date by the reign of Jeroboam of Israel (2 Kings 15:1), as it usually leaves out the kings of the north.

decisions.choice: fifty-two years: a reign that may include years shared with others
decisions.reason: This is one of the longest reigns of any king of Judah. For part of it his son Jotham ruled for him (verse 21), and the count may include years when he ruled beside his father.

decisions.choice: Jecoliah: the name as the scribes marked it to be read
decisions.reason: The written text and the form the scribes marked to be read aloud spell the queen mother's name slightly differently. Both name the same woman, called Jecoliah in 2 Kings 15:2.

decisions.choice: sixteen years old
decisions.reason: The wording of 2 Kings 15:2 is kept at each level, with the king's name added as the Hebrew has it.

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה אֲמַצְיָ֥הוּ אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he did the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh, according to all that had done Amaziah his father.
pieces: He did what was right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as his father Amaziah had done.

L.4: And he did the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, according to all that Amaziah his father had done.

R.4: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was right, just as his father Amaziah had done.

decisions.choice: as 2 Kings 15:3, without the high places
decisions.reason: The verdict is word for word that of 2 Kings 15:3. Kings goes on to say that the high places were not removed (15:4); Chronicles leaves that out and instead shows how Uzziah's faithfulness lasted only for a time (verses 5 and 16).

decisions.choice: according to all that Amaziah his father had done: a likeness that cuts both ways
decisions.reason: Amaziah too began well and then turned away (25:2, 14-16). The comparison prepares for Uzziah's own fall in verse 16.

decisions.choice: did the right in [the] eyes of / did what was right in the sight of / did what the LORD said was right
decisions.reason: The verdict formula has one wording at each level throughout these books.

records.source: וַיְהִי֙ לִדְרֹ֣שׁ אֱלֹהִ֔ים בִּימֵ֣י זְכַרְיָ֔הוּ הַמֵּבִ֖ין בִּרְאֹ֣ת הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וּבִימֵי֙ דָּרְשׁ֣וֹ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה הִצְלִיח֖וֹ הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: And he was to seek God in [the] days of Zechariah, the [one] giving understanding in the seeing of God; and in [the] days of his seeking Yahweh, made him prosper God.
pieces: He set himself to seek God during the lifetime of Zechariah, who taught him the fear of God. As long as he sought {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God gave him success.

L.5: And he sought God in the days of Zechariah, who instructed [him] in the fear of God; and in the days when he sought {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, God made him prosper.

R.5: Uzziah tried to follow God as long as Zechariah was alive. Zechariah taught him to respect and obey God. As long as Uzziah looked to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for help, God made him successful.

decisions.choice: in the fear of God
alternatives: who had understanding in the visions of God
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text as printed reads "in the seeing of God", which could mean that Zechariah understood visions from God. Many Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient Greek and Syriac translations read "in the fear of God"; the two words look very much alike in Hebrew. "The fear of God" fits a teacher who instructed the king, so it is followed here, but the printed reading, "who had understanding in the visions of God", is possible.

decisions.choice: seek God: turn to God in worship and trust
decisions.reason: To seek God, or seek Yahweh, is the mark of a faithful king in Chronicles (14:3; 15:12; 17:4). The verse twice ties Uzziah's success to his seeking, as the prophet told Asa: "if you seek him, he will be found by you" (15:2).

decisions.choice: Zechariah: a teacher of the king, otherwise unknown
decisions.reason: This Zechariah is not the prophet whose book is in the Bible, who lived after the exile, nor the priest killed under Joash (24:20-22). Like the priest Jehoiada for Joash (24:2), he guided the young king, and the verse implies that his influence waned or ended with his death.

decisions.choice: he was to seek God: he kept seeking, he set himself to seek
decisions.reason: The verb "to be" with "to seek" describes a settled course through a period of time: during Zechariah's days he made seeking God his practice.

decisions.choice: set himself to seek (Balanced); tried to follow, respect and obey (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the ongoing purpose (m4). Readable explains "seek" as following God and looking to him for help, and "the fear of God" as respecting and obeying him.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵא֙ וַיִּלָּ֣חֶם בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיִּפְרֹ֞ץ אֶת־ח֣וֹמַת גַּ֗ת וְאֵת֙ חוֹמַ֣ת יַבְנֵ֔ה וְאֵ֖ת חוֹמַ֣ת אַשְׁדּ֑וֹד וַיִּבְנֶ֣ה עָרִ֔ים בְּאַשְׁדּ֖וֹד וּבַפְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And he went out and fought against the Philistines and broke down [the] wall of Gath and [the] wall of Jabneh and [the] wall of Ashdod; and he built cities in Ashdod and among the Philistines.
pieces: He went out and made war on the Philistines, and broke down the walls of Gath, Jabneh and Ashdod. Then he built towns in the region of Ashdod and elsewhere among the Philistines.

L.6: And he went out and fought against the Philistines, and broke down the wall of Gath and the wall of Jabneh and the wall of Ashdod; and he built cities in Ashdod and among the Philistines.

R.6: Uzziah went to war against the Philistines. He broke down the walls around the cities of Gath, Jabneh and Ashdod. Then he built towns of his own near Ashdod and in other parts of the Philistines' land.

decisions.choice: Gath, Jabneh, Ashdod: Philistine cities on Judah's western side
decisions.reason: Gath and Ashdod were among the five chief Philistine cities (1 Samuel 6:17). Jabneh, near the coast, is called Jabneel in Joshua 15:11. Breaking their walls left them open to Judah.

decisions.choice: built cities in Ashdod: fortified towns in Ashdod's territory
decisions.reason: "In Ashdod" here means in the land around the city of Ashdod. Uzziah built or fortified towns there to hold the region.

decisions.choice: the region of Ashdod (Balanced); near Ashdod, the Philistines' land (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "in Ashdod" means (m2). Readable names Uzziah and adds "the cities of" before the names.

records.source: וַיַּעְזְרֵ֨הוּ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֜ים עַל־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֧ים וְעַל־הָֽעַרְבִ֛ים הַיֹּשְׁבִ֥ים בְּגוּר־בָּ֖עַל וְהַמְּעוּנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And helped him God against [the] Philistines and against the Arabs the [ones] dwelling in Gur-baal, and the Meunites.
pieces: God helped him against the Philistines, against the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal, and against the Meunites.

L.7: And God helped him against [the] Philistines and against the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal, and the Meunites.

R.7: God helped him fight the Philistines, the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal, and the Meunites.

decisions.choice: God helped him: the help his name speaks of
decisions.reason: The verb "help" is the root of the name Azariah, "Yahweh has helped", by which Kings knows this king. Chronicles comes back to it in verses 13 and 15: his strength came from God's help.

decisions.choice: the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal: desert tribes to the south
decisions.reason: Arab tribes of the desert south of Judah also appear in 17:11 and 21:16. Gur-baal is not named anywhere else, and where it lay is unknown.

decisions.choice: the Meunites: a people of the region south of the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: The Meunites are named beside the people of Mount Seir, the land of Edom (1 Chronicles 4:41-42). The name may come from the town of Maon or a place called Maan.

decisions.choice: against the Meunites (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins "and the Meunites" without repeating "against"; Balanced repeats it so the list reads clearly. Readable says "helped him fight".

records.source: וַיִּתְּנ֧וּ הָֽעַמּוֹנִ֛ים מִנְחָ֖ה לְעֻזִּיָּ֑הוּ וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ שְׁמוֹ֙ עַד־לְב֣וֹאמִצְרַ֔יִם כִּ֥י הֶחֱזִ֖יק עַד־לְמָֽעְלָה׃
records.gloss: And gave the Ammonites tribute to Uzziah, and went his name as far as [the] entrance of Egypt, for he became strong to upward.
pieces: The Ammonites brought tribute to Uzziah, and his fame reached all the way to the border of Egypt, because he had grown very strong.

L.8: And the Ammonites gave tribute to Uzziah, and his name went as far as the entrance of Egypt, for he became exceedingly strong.

R.8: The Ammonites paid Uzziah taxes to show they were under his rule. People heard about him as far away as the border of Egypt, because he had become very powerful.

decisions.choice: the Ammonites
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "the Meunites" here, which would continue the list of verse 7; the two names look alike in Hebrew. The Hebrew text is kept. Ammon lay east of the Jordan, and it paid tribute again to Uzziah's son Jotham (27:5).

decisions.choice: tribute: payment as a sign of submission
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a gift or a grain offering; given by one nation to another king, it is tribute, the payment of a people under his rule (17:11; 2 Samuel 8:2).

decisions.choice: his name went: his fame spread
decisions.reason: A person's name stands for his reputation. "The entrance of Egypt" is the way into Egypt, its border in the south-west.

decisions.choice: strong to upward: exceedingly strong
decisions.reason: The phrase means "to a high degree", as in 16:12 and 17:12.

decisions.choice: taxes to show they were under his rule
decisions.reason: Readable explains what tribute was (m2) and says the idiom "his name went" plainly.

records.source: וַיִּ֨בֶן עֻזִּיָּ֤הוּ מִגְדָּלִים֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם עַל־שַׁ֧עַר הַפִּנָּ֛ה וְעַל־שַׁ֥עַר הַגַּ֖יְא וְעַל־הַמִּקְצ֑וֹעַ וַֽיְחַזְּקֵֽם׃
records.gloss: And built Uzziah towers in Jerusalem at [the] gate of the corner and at [the] gate of the valley and at the angle, and he strengthened them.
pieces: In Jerusalem Uzziah built towers at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate and the Angle, and he fortified them.

L.9: And Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate and at the Valley Gate and at the Angle, and he fortified them.

R.9: Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem beside the Corner Gate, beside the Valley Gate and at the place where the wall turns, and he made them strong.

decisions.choice: the Corner Gate and the Valley Gate: gates in the walls of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The Corner Gate was at the north-west of the city; the wall between it and the Ephraim Gate had been broken down by Joash of Israel in Amaziah's day (25:23). The Valley Gate opened on the valley west and south of the city (Nehemiah 2:13; 3:13). Uzziah's towers repaired and strengthened the city's defenses.

decisions.choice: the Angle: a bend or buttress in the wall
decisions.reason: The word means a corner or turning. It names a place on the eastern wall near the palace in Nehemiah 3:19-25, where the line of the wall turned. Its exact place here is not certain.

decisions.choice: the place where the wall turns
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "the Angle" as a place name; Readable says what it was (m2).

records.source: וַיִּ֨בֶן מִגְדָּלִ֜ים בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר וַיַּחְצֹב֙ בֹּר֣וֹת רַבִּ֔ים כִּ֤י מִקְנֶה־רַּב֙ הָ֣יָה ל֔וֹ וּבַשְּׁפֵלָ֖ה וּבַמִּישׁ֑וֹר אִכָּרִ֣ים וְכֹֽרְמִ֗ים בֶּהָרִים֙ וּבַכַּרְמֶ֔ל כִּֽי־אֹהֵ֥ב אֲדָמָ֖ה הָיָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And he built towers in the wilderness and hewed cisterns many, for livestock much belonged to him; and in the Shephelah and in the plain, farmers and vinedressers in the mountains and in the fruitful land, for loving [the] ground he was.
pieces: He built towers in the wilderness and cut out many cisterns, for he had large herds in the Shephelah and on the plain. He had farmers and vinedressers working in the hill country and the fertile fields, for he loved the soil.

L.10: And he built towers in the wilderness and cut out many cisterns, for he had much livestock, in the Shephelah and in the plain; [he had] farmers and vinedressers in the hills and in the fruitful land, for he was a lover of the soil.

R.10: He built watchtowers in the desert and dug many large pits in the rock to hold water, because he had many cattle and sheep in the western foothills and on the high plain. He had people working his fields and his vineyards in the hills and in the good farmland, because he loved working the land.

decisions.choice: towers and cisterns: watchtowers and water storage for herds
decisions.reason: In the dry south a tower guarded flocks and travelers, and a cistern cut into the rock stored the winter rain for the dry season. Remains of such towers and cisterns from the time of the kings have been found in the Negev.

decisions.choice: in the Shephelah and in the plain: where the livestock were kept
decisions.reason: The phrase most naturally belongs with the livestock just named. It could also begin the next clause, placing the farmers there as well.

decisions.choice: the Shephelah and the plain: the low hills west of Judah and the tableland east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The Shephelah is the band of low hills between the hill country of Judah and the coastal plain (Joshua 15:33). "The plain" usually names the high tableland east of the Dead Sea (Deuteronomy 3:10), though it may mean any level ground.

decisions.choice: the fruitful land: garden land, not the mountain named Carmel
decisions.reason: The word is the same as the name of Mount Carmel, but it is also a common noun for fertile, cultivated land (Isaiah 29:17; Jeremiah 2:7). The northern Carmel lay in Israel, not Judah, so the common sense fits here.

decisions.choice: he loved the soil: he cared for farming
decisions.reason: The word for "soil" is the ground that is tilled (Genesis 2:5). The king took a personal interest in his farms and herds.

decisions.choice: [he had] (Literal); He had (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew lists the farmers and vinedressers without a verb; English supplies "he had". Readable explains cisterns as pits in the rock for water and the Shephelah as the western foothills.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י לְעֻזִּיָּ֡הוּ חַיִל֩ עֹשֵׂ֨ה מִלְחָמָ֜ה יוֹצְאֵ֧י צָבָ֣א לִגְד֗וּד בְּמִסְפַּר֙ פְּקֻדָּתָ֔ם בְּיַד֙ יְעִיאֵ֣ל הַסּוֹפֵ֔ר וּמַעֲשֵׂיָ֖הוּ הַשּׁוֹטֵ֑ר עַ֚ל יַד־חֲנַנְיָ֔הוּ מִשָּׂרֵ֖י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And belonged to Uzziah an army doing war, going out [to the] army by band, by [the] number of their muster by [the] hand of Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer, under [the] hand of Hananiah, of [the] commanders of the king.
pieces: Uzziah had an army ready for battle, which went out to war in divisions, according to the numbers in the muster made by Jeiel the secretary and Maaseiah the official, who worked under Hananiah, one of the king's commanders.

L.11: And Uzziah had an army for making war, going out to war by bands, according to the number of their muster by the hand of Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the official, under the hand of Hananiah, one of the commanders of the king.

R.11: Uzziah had an army trained for battle. They went out to war in groups. Jeiel the secretary and Maaseiah the official had counted the soldiers and listed them in their groups. Hananiah, one of the king's commanders, was in charge of them.

decisions.choice: by bands: in organized units
decisions.reason: The word often means a raiding band, but here it names the units into which the army was divided for service.

decisions.choice: the scribe and the official: royal officials who kept the muster
decisions.reason: The scribe was a royal secretary who kept written records; the other was an official who helped organize the people and the army (Deuteronomy 20:5-9). Together they enrolled the soldiers.

decisions.choice: Jeiel: the name as the scribes marked it to be read
decisions.reason: The written text and the form marked to be read aloud spell this name slightly differently; both name the same man.

decisions.choice: by the hand of, under the hand of: carried out by, under the authority of
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for the person who acts and the one who directs: Jeiel and Maaseiah did the counting, under Hananiah's command.

decisions.choice: the scribe (Literal); the secretary (Balanced, Readable); the official; commanders
decisions.reason: As in Kings, Literal says "scribe" and Balanced and Readable "secretary" for the royal record-keeper. The second title is "official" at every level, as in Deuteronomy 16:18 and 2 Chronicles 19:11. The king's officers in a military setting are "commanders" at every level.

records.heading: Uzziah's army and his pride

records.source: כֹּ֠ל מִסְפַּ֞ר רָאשֵׁ֤י הָאָבוֹת֙ לְגִבּ֣וֹרֵי חָ֔יִל אַלְפַּ֖יִם וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: All [the] number of [the] heads of the fathers of mighty [men] of strength [was] two thousand and six hundred.
pieces: The total number of family heads over the mighty warriors was 2,600.

L.12: The whole number of the heads of the fathers' [houses], mighty men of valor, [was] 2,600.

R.12: There were 2,600 family leaders in charge of these brave warriors.

decisions.choice: heads of the fathers: leaders of the family groups
decisions.reason: The army was organized by families, and the heads of the father's houses led the men of their families (1 Chronicles 7:40).

decisions.choice: two thousand: the numbers as given
decisions.reason: On the size of numbers given in thousands, see the note at Numbers 1:21; here, as there, the text is read as giving the number.

decisions.choice: mighty men of valor: tried and able fighting men
decisions.reason: The phrase names strong, capable warriors, as in 13:3 and 14:7.

decisions.choice: over the mighty warriors (Balanced); in charge of (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew links the family heads and the warriors with a simple "of"; Balanced and Readable say that the heads led the warriors.

records.source: וְעַל־יָדָם֩ חֵ֨יל צָבָ֜א שְׁלֹ֧שׁ מֵא֣וֹת אֶ֗לֶף וְשִׁבְעַ֤ת אֲלָפִים֙ וַחֲמֵ֣שׁ מֵא֔וֹת עוֹשֵׂ֥י מִלְחָמָ֖ה בְּכֹ֣חַ חָ֑יִל לַעְזֹ֥ר לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עַל־הָאוֹיֵֽב׃
records.gloss: And under their hand [was the] force of [the] army, three hundred thousand and seven thousand and five hundred, doing war with power of strength, to help the king against the enemy.
pieces: Under their command was an army of 307,500 men, a powerful fighting force ready to help the king against his enemies.

L.13: And under their hand [was] an army force of 307,500, making war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy.

R.13: They commanded an army of 307,500 men. These soldiers fought with great strength and helped the king against his enemies.

decisions.choice: thousand: the numbers as given
decisions.reason: As in verse 12: on the size of numbers given in thousands, see the note at Numbers 1:21.

decisions.choice: to help the king: the word of help again
decisions.reason: The army's task is put in the word that runs through this chapter (verses 7 and 15) and lies behind the king's other name, Azariah. God helped Uzziah, and his army was there to help him too.

decisions.choice: under their hand: under their command
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for authority: the family heads of verse 12 led these troops.

decisions.choice: men; his enemies
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "men" to the total, as in 14:7, and say "his enemies" for "the enemy", meaning any enemy who came against him.

records.source: וַיָּכֶן֩ לָהֶ֨ם עֻזִּיָּ֜הוּ לְכָל־הַצָּבָ֗א מָגִנִּ֤ים וּרְמָחִים֙ וְכ֣וֹבָעִ֔ים וְשִׁרְיֹנ֖וֹת וּקְשָׁת֑וֹת וּלְאַבְנֵ֖י קְלָעִֽים׃
records.gloss: And prepared for them Uzziah, for all the army, shields and spears and helmets and coats of mail and bows and for stones of slings.
pieces: Uzziah provided the whole army with shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows and stones for slinging.

L.14: And Uzziah prepared for them, for all the army, shields and spears and helmets and coats of mail and bows and stones for slings.

R.14: Uzziah gave the whole army shields, spears and helmets, armor to protect their bodies, bows, and stones to throw with slings.

decisions.choice: Uzziah prepared for all the army: weapons supplied by the king
decisions.reason: In earlier times soldiers often brought their own weapons (Judges 20:16; 1 Samuel 13:19-22). Here the king arms the whole army from his own stores, a sign of his wealth and strength.

decisions.choice: shields; coats of mail
decisions.reason: The shield here is the smaller round shield (14:7). The coat of mail was body armor made of small plates or scales, like Goliath's (1 Samuel 17:5, 38).

decisions.choice: stones for slings: stones shaped or chosen for slinging
decisions.reason: The sling was a strip of leather or cloth used to hurl stones with great force and accuracy (Judges 20:16; 1 Samuel 17:40). Stones made ready for it were part of an army's stores.

decisions.choice: armor to protect their bodies
decisions.reason: Readable says what a coat of mail was.

records.source: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ׀בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם חִשְּׁבֹנ֜וֹת מַחֲשֶׁ֣בֶת חוֹשֵׁ֗ב לִהְי֤וֹת עַל־הַמִּגְדָּלִים֙ וְעַל־הַפִּנּ֔וֹת לִירוֹא֙ בַּֽחִצִּ֔ים וּבָאֲבָנִ֖ים גְּדֹל֑וֹת וַיֵּצֵ֤א שְׁמוֹ֙ עַד־לְמֵ֣רָח֔וֹק כִּֽי־הִפְלִ֥יא לְהֵעָזֵ֖ר עַ֥ד כִּֽי־חָזָֽק׃
records.gloss: And he made in Jerusalem devices, [the] device of [a] deviser, to be on the towers and on the corners, to shoot with arrows and with stones great; and went out his name as far as to from afar, for he made wonderful to be helped until that he was strong.
pieces: In Jerusalem he made devices designed by skilled inventors, to be set on the towers and the corners of the walls for shooting arrows and large stones. His fame spread far and wide, for he was wonderfully helped until he became strong.

L.15: And he made in Jerusalem devices, the invention of an inventor, to be on the towers and on the corners, to shoot arrows and great stones. And his name went out as far as to a distance, for he was marvelously helped until he was strong.

R.15: In Jerusalem he had skilled men design new kinds of equipment for war. These were put on the towers and the corners of the walls, so that soldiers could shoot arrows and throw large stones from them. People in faraway places heard about Uzziah. God helped him in wonderful ways until he became very powerful.

decisions.choice: devices, the invention of an inventor: some new kind of defense on the walls
alternatives: engines that shot arrows and threw stones
decisions.reason: The three words come from one root meaning "to think out, devise", and stress the cleverness of the work. What the devices were is not certain. They may have been machines that shot arrows and hurled stones, or frames and shields built out from the battlements, from behind which defenders could shoot arrows and drop or throw stones on attackers below.

decisions.choice: he made wonderful to be helped: he was helped in a wonderful way
decisions.reason: The verb "make wonderful" with "to be helped" means that his help was extraordinary. The one who helped is not named here, but verse 7 has said it: God helped him.

decisions.choice: until he was strong: the turning point of the reign
decisions.reason: "Until" marks a limit. The help lasted until he became strong, and the next verse begins with his strength: "when he was strong" his heart grew proud. The words "help" and "strength" also echo his two names, Azariah and Uzziah.

decisions.choice: his name went out to a distance: his fame spread far
decisions.reason: As in verse 8, "name" means reputation.

decisions.choice: God helped him
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the helper, as verse 7 does (m2), and turns the devices into equipment that skilled men designed and soldiers used.

records.source: וּכְחֶזְקָת֗וֹ גָּבַ֤הּ לִבּוֹ֙ עַד־לְהַשְׁחִ֔ית וַיִּמְעַ֖ל בַּיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל־הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה לְהַקְטִ֖יר עַל־מִזְבַּ֥ח הַקְּטֹֽרֶת׃
records.gloss: And as his being strong was high his heart to destroy, and he acted unfaithfully against Yahweh his God, and he went into [the] temple of Yahweh to make smoke on [the] altar of the incense.
pieces: But when he had become strong, his heart grew proud, to his own ruin. He was unfaithful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God, and he went into the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to burn incense on the incense altar.

L.16: But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up, to [his] destruction, and he acted unfaithfully against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God, and went into the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to burn incense on the altar of incense.

R.16: But once Uzziah became powerful, he grew proud, and that led to his ruin. He was unfaithful to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God. He went into the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to burn incense on the incense altar himself.

decisions.choice: his heart was high: he became proud
decisions.reason: A high heart is pride (Proverbs 16:5, 18; Ezekiel 28:2, 5). The same words are used of Jehoshaphat in a good sense, "his heart was lifted up in the ways of Yahweh", meaning he took courage in them (17:6). Here they mean arrogance, as with Hezekiah later (32:25).

decisions.choice: to destroy: to his ruin
decisions.reason: The verb means to ruin or destroy, and also to act corruptly. The phrase can mean his pride led to his own destruction, or that it went so far that he acted corruptly. The first fits the story that follows.

decisions.choice: acted unfaithfully: broke faith with God
decisions.reason: This verb is a key word of Chronicles for breaking faith with God, used of Saul (1 Chronicles 10:13) and of Judah before the exile (1 Chronicles 9:1; 2 Chronicles 36:14). It describes taking what belongs to God, here the holy service kept for the priests.

decisions.choice: the temple; the altar of incense: the main hall of the house of God
decisions.reason: The altar of incense stood in the main hall, in front of the most holy place. Only priests of Aaron's line might burn incense on it, morning and evening (Exodus 30:1-10). When others tried to offer incense, judgment fell (Numbers 16:35; 17:5).

decisions.choice: Uzziah; himself
decisions.reason: Readable names the king, says "grew proud" for the picture of a high heart, and adds "himself" to show that the king meant to do the priests' work, which verse 18 makes plain.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֥א אַחֲרָ֖יו עֲזַרְיָ֣הוּ הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וְעִמּ֞וֹ כֹּהֲנִ֧ים׀לַיהוָ֛ה שְׁמוֹנִ֖ים בְּנֵי־חָֽיִל׃
records.gloss: And went after him Azariah the priest, and with him priests of Yahweh, eighty, sons of strength.
pieces: Azariah the priest went in after him, along with eighty priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, men of courage.

L.17: And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him [were] priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, eighty, men of valor.

R.17: Azariah the priest went in after him, together with eighty other priests of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They were brave men.

decisions.choice: Azariah the priest: not the king
decisions.reason: This Azariah is the chief priest (verse 20). His name is the one Kings uses for King Uzziah (2 Kings 15:1), but here it names the priest who stands against the king. Which Azariah of the priestly line he was is not certain (compare 1 Chronicles 5:36-40).

decisions.choice: sons of strength: brave, able men
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of warriors (1 Samuel 18:17), but here it means men of courage. It took courage to oppose a powerful king; under Joash a priest who spoke out had been stoned (24:20-22).

decisions.choice: other
decisions.reason: Readable adds "other" so it is clear the eighty went in with Azariah.

records.source: וַיַּעַמְד֞וּ עַל־עֻזִּיָּ֣הוּ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ לֹא־לְךָ֣ עֻזִּיָּ֗הוּ לְהַקְטִיר֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה כִּ֣י לַכֹּהֲנִ֧ים בְּנֵי־אַהֲרֹ֛ן הַמְקֻדָּשִׁ֖ים לְהַקְטִ֑יר צֵ֤א מִן־הַמִּקְדָּשׁ֙ כִּ֣י מָעַ֔לְתָּ וְלֹֽא־לְךָ֥ לְכָב֖וֹד מֵיְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And they stood against Uzziah the king and said to him, Not to you, Uzziah, to make smoke to Yahweh, for to the priests, [the] sons of Aaron, the [ones] consecrated to make smoke; go out from the sanctuary, for you have acted unfaithfully, and not to you for honor from Yahweh God.
pieces: They confronted King Uzziah and said to him, "It is not your place, Uzziah, to burn incense to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That belongs to the priests, the sons of Aaron, who have been set apart to burn incense. Leave the sanctuary, for you have been unfaithful, and this will bring you no honor from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God."

L.18: And they stood against Uzziah the king and said to him, "[It is] not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense. Go out from the sanctuary, for you have acted unfaithfully, and [it is] not for your honor from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God."

R.18: They stood in front of King Uzziah to stop him. They said, "Uzziah, you have no right to burn incense to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Only the priests, who come from Aaron's family, may do that. They have been set apart to burn incense. Get out of this holy place! You have been unfaithful to God, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God will not honor you for this."

decisions.choice: for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated: the law of the priesthood
decisions.reason: The law gave the burning of incense to Aaron and his sons (Exodus 30:7-8; Numbers 18:7). After Korah's rebellion, the bronze from the censers was made a sign that no one who was not of Aaron's line should come near to burn incense before Yahweh (Numbers 17:5). Consecrated means set apart for holy service (Exodus 29:1).

decisions.choice: stood against: confronted, opposed
decisions.reason: To stand against someone is to oppose them face to face. The priests stood in the king's way.

decisions.choice: not to you for honor: it will bring you no honor
decisions.reason: The words are short in Hebrew. They mean that what he is doing will not win him honor from God; instead it will bring disgrace, as the next verse shows.

decisions.choice: the sanctuary: the holy place
decisions.reason: The word means the holy place, here the temple building where only priests might go.

decisions.choice: confronted; set apart (Balanced); stood in front of him to stop him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "set apart" for "consecrated". Readable says what standing against him meant, adds "to God" after "unfaithful", and turns the last clause into a plain statement.

records.source: וַיִּזְעַף֙ עֻזִּיָּ֔הוּ וּבְיָד֥וֹ מִקְטֶ֖רֶת לְהַקְטִ֑יר וּבְזַעְפּ֣וֹ עִם־הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים וְ֠הַצָּרַעַת זָרְחָ֨ה בְמִצְח֜וֹ לִפְנֵ֤י הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה מֵעַ֖ל לְמִזְבַּ֥ח הַקְּטֹֽרֶת׃
records.gloss: And was angry Uzziah, and in his hand [was] a censer to make smoke; and in his being angry with the priests, and the scale disease shone out on his forehead before the priests in [the] house of Yahweh, from beside [the] altar of the incense.
pieces: Uzziah became furious. He had a censer in his hand ready to burn incense, and while he raged at the priests, a serious skin disease broke out on his forehead, there in front of the priests in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, beside the altar of incense.

L.19: And Uzziah was angry, and in his hand [was] a censer to burn incense; and when he was angry with the priests, the scale disease broke out on his forehead before the priests in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, beside the altar of incense.

R.19: Uzziah was holding a censer, ready to burn incense, and he became very angry. While he was raging at the priests, a serious skin disease suddenly appeared on his forehead. It happened right there in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, beside the incense altar, while the priests watched.

decisions.choice: scale disease: a skin disease that made a person unclean, not modern leprosy
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in Leviticus 13-14 for a group of skin conditions that made a person unclean and kept him away from the holy things. It is not the same as leprosy as known today. 2 Kings 15:5 says that Yahweh struck the king with it; Chronicles tells how it came about.

decisions.choice: shone out: broke out suddenly and plainly
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the sun rising (Genesis 32:32). The disease appeared all at once, in plain sight of everyone, on the king's forehead.

decisions.choice: a censer: a pan for carrying burning coals and incense
decisions.reason: A censer held live coals on which incense was burned (Ezekiel 8:11; compare the fire pans of Leviticus 16:12). It was the priests' vessel for this service.

decisions.choice: before the priests, beside the altar of incense: judgment in the holy place
decisions.reason: The disease struck at the very altar the king meant to use, before the priests who had warned him. As with Miriam (Numbers 12:10), the mark of the disease came as a sign of God's judgment.

decisions.choice: scale disease (Literal); serious skin disease (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording for the disease follows Leviticus 13 and 2 Kings 15:5. Readable puts the censer first and says "while the priests watched" for "before the priests".

records.source: וַיִּ֣פֶן אֵלָ֡יו עֲזַרְיָהוּ֩ כֹהֵ֨ן הָרֹ֜אשׁ וְכָל־הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים וְהִנֵּה־ה֤וּא מְצֹרָע֙ בְּמִצְח֔וֹ וַיַּבְהִל֖וּהוּ מִשָּׁ֑ם וְגַם־הוּא֙ נִדְחַ֣ף לָצֵ֔את כִּ֥י נִגְּע֖וֹ יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And turned to him Azariah the chief priest and all the priests, and look, he [was] diseased on his forehead; and they hurried him from there, and also he himself hastened to go out, for had struck him Yahweh.
pieces: When Azariah the chief priest and all the priests looked at him, there on his forehead was the skin disease! They rushed him out of there, and he himself hurried to leave, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck him.

L.20: And Azariah the chief priest and all the priests turned to him, and look, he [had] scale disease on his forehead! And they rushed him out from there, and he himself also hurried to go out, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck him.

R.20: Azariah the chief priest and all the other priests looked at him and saw the disease on his forehead. They quickly made him leave the temple. Uzziah himself was in a hurry to get out, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck him with the disease.

decisions.choice: look: what the priests saw
decisions.reason: The word draws the reader into the priests' sight: as they turned, there it was.

decisions.choice: they hurried him out, and he hurried to go: the unclean had to leave the holy place
decisions.reason: A person with this disease was unclean and had to live outside the camp (Leviticus 13:45-46; Numbers 5:2-3). The priests rushed him out, and the king, struck and afraid, now went quickly himself.

decisions.choice: Yahweh had struck him: as 2 Kings 15:5
decisions.reason: Kings uses the same verb: "Yahweh struck the king". Chronicles shows when and why it happened.

decisions.choice: the chief priest: the head of the priests
decisions.reason: "The head priest" is the high priest, the one who led the priesthood (19:11; 24:11).

decisions.choice: the temple; with the disease
decisions.reason: Readable says where "there" was and what the king was struck with. Balanced and Readable say "looked at" for "turned to".

records.source: וַיְהִי֩ עֻזִּיָּ֨הוּ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ מְצֹרָ֣ע׀עַד־י֣וֹם מוֹת֗וֹ וַיֵּ֜שֶׁב בֵּ֤ית הַֽחָפְשִׁית֙ מְצֹרָ֔ע כִּ֥י נִגְזַ֖ר מִבֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וְיוֹתָ֤ם בְּנוֹ֙ עַל־בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שׁוֹפֵ֖ט אֶת־עַ֥ם הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And was Uzziah the king diseased until [the] day of his death, and he dwelt [in the] house of the freedom, diseased, for he was cut off from [the] house of Yahweh; and Jotham his son [was] over [the] house of the king, judging [the] people of the land.
pieces: King Uzziah had a serious skin disease until the day he died. He lived in a separate house because of the disease, for he was shut out of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, while his son Jotham was in charge of the palace and governed the people of the land.

L.21: And Uzziah the king was [one] with scale disease until the day of his death, and he lived in the separate house, [one] with scale disease, for he was cut off from the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and Jotham his son [was] over the house of the king, judging the people of the land.

R.21: King Uzziah had the serious skin disease until the day he died. Because of it he lived in a house by himself, and he was not allowed to go into the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. His son Jotham was in charge of the palace and ruled the people of the land.

decisions.choice: as 2 Kings 15:5, with a reason added
decisions.reason: The verse follows 2 Kings 15:5. Kings begins "Yahweh struck the king", which Chronicles has already told (verse 20). Chronicles repeats "diseased" and adds "for he was cut off from the house of Yahweh", and it says "Jotham his son" and "the house of the king" where Kings has "Jotham the king's son" and "the house".

decisions.choice: the house of freedom: a separate house, where he lived apart
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 15:5: the word is related to "free", so the phrase is literally "the house of freedom" or "of release". It may mean a house where the king lived released from his duties, or simply a house set apart because of his disease. Its exact sense is not known. The written text and the form marked to be read aloud spell the word slightly differently, with the same sense.

decisions.choice: cut off from the house of Yahweh: shut out of the temple
decisions.reason: Being unclean, he could no longer go to the temple at all (Leviticus 13:46). The king who forced his way into the holy place was barred from the whole house of God for the rest of his life.

decisions.choice: over the house of the king, judging the people of the land: running the palace and governing Judah
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 15:5, Jotham ruled for his father until he became king himself (27:1).

decisions.choice: scale disease (Literal); serious skin disease (Balanced, Readable); separate house / a house by himself
decisions.reason: The wording follows 2 Kings 15:5. Balanced says "because of the disease" for the repeated "diseased", and "shut out" for "cut off"; Readable says he was not allowed to go into the temple.

records.source: וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י עֻזִּיָּ֔הוּ הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאֲחֲרֹנִ֑יםכָּתַ֛ב יְשַֽׁעְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־אָמ֖וֹץ הַנָּבִֽיא׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Uzziah, the first and the last, wrote Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet.
pieces: The rest of the acts of Uzziah, from first to last, were written down by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.

L.22: And the rest of the matters of Uzziah, the first and the last, Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet wrote.

R.22: Everything else Uzziah did, from beginning to end, was written down by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.

decisions.choice: Isaiah son of Amoz the prophet wrote: a source different from 2 Kings 15:6
decisions.reason: Kings points to "the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah" for Azariah's other acts. Chronicles names the prophet Isaiah as the writer, as it names prophets for other kings (9:29; 12:15). Isaiah began his work under Uzziah and saw his vision of the Lord in the year Uzziah died (Isaiah 1:1; 6:1). The book of Isaiah says little about Uzziah's acts, so this was probably a separate writing that has not survived; compare 32:32, "the vision of Isaiah".

decisions.choice: the first and the last: the whole reign
decisions.reason: As in 9:29 and 16:11, the phrase covers all of his acts, from beginning to end.

decisions.choice: were written down by the prophet Isaiah
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew order, with the acts first and "Isaiah wrote" at the end. Balanced and Readable turn it around so the sentence reads easily, using the wording of the sources formula.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב עֻזִּיָּ֜הוּ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַיִּקְבְּר֨וּ אֹת֤וֹ עִם־אֲבֹתָיו֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֤ה הַקְּבוּרָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לַמְּלָכִ֔ים כִּ֥י אָמְר֖וּ מְצוֹרָ֣ע ה֑וּא וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יוֹתָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And lay down Uzziah with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in [the] field of the burial which [belonged] to the kings, for they said, Diseased [is] he; and reigned Jotham his son in his place.
pieces: Then Uzziah rested with his ancestors, and they buried him near his ancestors in the burial field that belonged to the kings, for they said, "He has a serious skin disease." His son Jotham became king in his place.

L.23: And Uzziah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of burial that [belonged] to the kings, for they said, "He [is one] with scale disease." And Jotham his son reigned in his place.

R.23: Then Uzziah died. He was buried near his ancestors, in a field of graves that belonged to the kings, because people said, "He has a serious skin disease." His son Jotham became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The death formula of these books, as in 2 Kings 15:7.

decisions.choice: in the field of burial of the kings: where 2 Kings 15:7 says "in the City of David"
decisions.reason: Kings says only that he was buried with his fathers in the City of David. Chronicles adds that he was laid in a field belonging to the royal burial ground, not in the royal tombs themselves, because of his disease. He was near his fathers, but still set apart.

decisions.choice: for they said, He has skin disease: unclean even in death
decisions.reason: His disease made him unclean to the end, and the people would not lay him in the tombs with the other kings. The verse gives their reason in their own words.

decisions.choice: near his ancestors (Balanced, Readable); rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "near" for the second "with his fathers", since he was buried beside the royal tombs, not in them (m2). The death formula keeps its wording at each level; Readable says "was buried" and "people said" for "they buried" and "they said".
